messages:
alex: FYI customer tenant `acme-corp` is seeing a sudden flood of 429s and billing warnings. Started ~10:02 UTC after the midnight rate-limiter rollout. @oncall please take a look :eyes:

maria: Thanks. Any request IDs or logs? Is it global or single region?

alex: single region (us-west-2). Quick log tail from the proxy: 
```
[10:03:12] error=rate_limiter: tenant=acme-corp allow=false bucket_tokens=0 refill_unit=minute refill_amount=60 window=1m
[10:03:12] error=auth: token ok tenant=acme-corp req_id=ry47... status=429
[10:03:13] warn=burst_allowed=false configured_burst=100
```

sam: Hmm refill_unit=minute stands out. IIRC the previous config used seconds. Did the rollout switch units?

raj: We had a config-stage change last night to normalize units to 's'|'m' but the parser fallback default is weird if unspecified. Could be misread as minutes instead of seconds for some tenants.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: rate-limiter-config v4.2.1 -> v4.3.0 by @infra at 2024-08-30T00:01:10Z (canary passed)

support-bot: Customer ticket #54120: "sudden quota exhaustion causing 429s, impacting API UX, billing spike". Priority P1.

maria: Can someone reproduce quickly on staging with tenant config from prod? If it's minute vs second mismatch that explains the sudden token exhaustion.

alex: Repro steps I'm trying: 
1) apply the prod config snippet for acme-corp locally
2) run a 1k qps burst for 30s against the limiter endpoint
Command: 
```bash
./scripts/limiter_load_test --tenant acme-corp --qps 1000 --duration 30s --target http://localhost:8080/limit
```
Observed: ~50% requests 429 after ~10s.

raj: Adding the config snippet I pulled from the rollout: 
```yaml
tenant: acme-corp
policy:
  refill_amount: 60
  refill_unit: minute  # v4.3.0 set to `minute` by mistake for some codepaths
  burst: 100
  window: 1m
```

sam: OK that would refill 60 tokens/min (1 token/sec) not 60 tokens/sec. If previously it was interpreted as seconds tenants had much higher sustained QPS. That matches the spike.

maria: Proposed quick mitigation: rollback the rate-limiter-config to v4.2.1 for us-west-2 and temporarily increase `burst` for acme-corp to 500 until fix deploy. Thoughts?

alex: I can push a regional rollback for the config in 5 minutes. Also opening a temp tenant override: 
```json
{ "tenant": "acme-corp", "overrides": { "burst": 500 } }
```

raj: Patch idea: make the parser accept both full word and shorthand, and default to seconds if ambiguous. Also add a CI check that prevents unit regressions. I'll open a PR.

sam: Monitoring queries to watch: 
PromQL: 
```promql
sum by (tenant) (rate(limiter_allowed_total{tenant="acme-corp"}[1m]))
sum by (tenant) (rate(limiter_denied_total{tenant="acme-corp"}[1m]))
```
Set an alert if denied rate spikes > 5% of allowed for 5m.

maria: alex, proceed with rollback and tenant override. raj, please land the parser patch asap and get a canary. After rollback, let's confirm with a production-sim load test before removing override.

alex: Rolling back now. Patch the override. I'll paste ops runbook steps after done.

deploy-bot: rollback started: rate-limiter-config v4.3.0 -> v4.2.1 in us-west-2

alex: Rollback complete at 10:12 UTC. Preliminary stats: denied rate for acme-corp dropped from 38% -> 2% within 30s.

maria: Great. Action items: 1) raj open PR for unit parsing + CI test. 2) infra to add canary validation for config unit fields. 3) support to follow up with customer and waive excess billing for the window. 4) postmortem with timeline.

raj: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3487 "rate-limiter: normalize refill_unit, default to seconds + unit CI". Adding automated test that simulates config with `minute`/`m`/`s` edgecases.

sam: I'll add the alert rule tweak and create a dashboard tile for per-tenant denied/allowed ratio.

support-bot: Noted — support will liaise with acme-corp and flag billing adjustment in ticket #54120.

maria: OK closing the incident channel here, moving action items to postmortem doc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
